brontosaurus:enwiki:5.title: Brontosaurus (Skull correction, resurgent discoveries, and reassessment)

facts.statement: The animal is classified under the genus Brontosaurus.
facts.quote: taxon: Brontosaurus

facts.statement: The genus Brontosaurus was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879.
facts.quote: authority: Marsh, 1879

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Brontosaurus excelsus.
facts.quote: type_species: Brontosaurus excelsus

facts.statement: Two other species, B. parvus and B. yahnahpin, were named in 1902 and 1994 respectively.
facts.quote: subdivision: * Brontosaurus parvus (Peterson & Gilmore, 1902) Brontosaurus yahnahpin (Filla & Redman, 1994)

facts.statement: Brontosaurus fossils date to the Late Jurassic, specifically the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian to Tithonian)

facts.statement: The type species B. excelsus was based on a partial skeleton without a skull found in Como Bluff, Wyoming.
facts.quote: It was described by American paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879, the type species being dubbed B. excelsus, based on a partial skeleton lacking a skull found in Como Bluff, Wyoming.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus lived between 156 and 146 million years ago in the Morrison Formation of Utah and Wyoming.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus lived about 156 to 146 million years ago (mya) during the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian ages in the Morrison Formation of what is now Utah and Wyoming.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus ( ; literally thunder lizard, from the Greek words βροντή , thunder, and σαῦρος , lizard) is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur

facts.statement: Fossils show Brontosaurus was large, long-necked, quadrupedal, and had a long tail ending in a whip-like structure.
facts.quote: The anatomy of Brontosaurus is well known, with fossils demonstrating that it was large, long-necked, and quadrupedal with a long tail terminating in a whip-like structure.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus had extremely robust and heavily built cervical vertebrae compared to its relatives Diplodocus and Barosaurus.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae are notably extremely robust and heavily built, in contrast to its lightly built relatives Diplodocus and Barosaurus.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus had short, stout forelimbs and elongated, thick hindlimbs supported by heavy shoulder and pelvic girdles.
facts.quote: The forelimbs were short and stout whereas the hindlimbs were elongated and thick, supported respectively by a heavily built shoulder girdle and pelvis.

facts.statement: The largest species, B. excelsus, reached lengths of 21 to 23 meters and weighed 15 to 20 tonnes.
facts.quote: Several size estimates have been made, with the largest species B. excelsus reaching up to 21 - 23 m from head to tail and weighing in at 15 - 20 t

facts.statement: The smaller species B. parvus reached a maximum length of 19 meters.
facts.quote: whereas the smaller B. parvus only got up to 19 m long.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus is classified within the family Diplodocidae.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus has been classified within the family Diplodocidae

facts.statement: Brontosaurus belongs to the subfamily Apatosaurinae, which includes only Brontosaurus and Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus is a genus in the subfamily Apatosaurinae, which includes only it and Apatosaurus

facts.statement: Some paleontologists still debate whether Brontosaurus is a valid genus or a synonym of Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: However, the status of Brontosaurus is still uncertain, with some paleontologists still considering it a synonym of Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: The type specimen was collected from the Morrison Formation at Como Bluff, Wyoming, by William Harlow Reed.
facts.quote: The specimen was collected from Morrison Formation rocks at Como Bluff, Wyoming by William Harlow Reed.

facts.statement: Marsh named the new species Brontosaurus excelsus, derived from Greek words for thunder and lizard and Latin for noble or high.
facts.quote: He identified it as belonging to an entirely new genus and species, which he named Brontosaurus excelsus, meaning "thunder lizard", from the Greek /βροντη meaning "thunder" and /σαυρος meaning "lizard", and from the Latin excelsus, "noble" or "high".

facts.statement: In 1880, Reed collected another partial postcranial skeleton near Como Bluff with well-preserved limb elements.
facts.quote: A year later in 1880, another partial postcranial Brontosaurus skeleton was collected near Como Bluff by Reed, including well-preserved limb elements.

facts.statement: Marsh named a second skeleton B. amplus in 1881, but it was considered a synonym of B. excelsus in 2015.
facts.quote: Marsh named this second skeleton Brontosaurus amplus ("large thunder lizard") in 1881, but it was considered a synonym of B. excelsus in 2015.

facts.statement: In August 1883, Marshall P. Felch collected a partial skull at Garden Park, Colorado, and sent it to Yale.
facts.quote: In August 1883, Marshall P. Felch collected a disarticulated partial skull (USNM V 5730) of a sauropod further south in the Felch Quarry at Garden Park, Colorado and sent the specimen to Yale.

facts.statement: Marsh referred the Felch skull to B. excelsus and used it in reconstructions published in 1891 and 1896.
facts.quote: Marsh referred the skull to B. excelsus, later featuring it in a skeletal reconstruction of the B. excelsus type specimen in 1891 and the illustration was featured again in Marsh's landmark publication, The Dinosaurs of North America, in 1896.

facts.statement: The Yale Peabody Museum mounted a B. excelsus skeleton in 1931 using a skull based on Marsh's reconstruction of the Felch Quarry specimen.
facts.quote: At the Yale Peabody Museum, the skeleton of Brontosaurus excelsus was mounted in 1931 with a skull based on the Marsh reconstruction of the Felch Quarry skull.

facts.statement: In 1998 and supported in 2020, researchers suggested the Felch Quarry skull belongs to Brachiosaurus rather than Brontosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1998, the Felch Quarry skull that Marsh included in his 1896 skeletal restoration was suggested to belong to Brachiosaurus instead and this was supported in 2020 with a redescription of the brachiosaurid material found at the Felch Quarry.

facts.statement: In 1901, William Harlow Reed collected a partial juvenile Brontosaurus skeleton (CM 566) during an expedition in Wyoming.
facts.quote: During a Carnegie Museum expedition to Wyoming in 1901, William Harlow Reed collected another Brontosaurus skeleton, a partial postcranial skeleton of a young juvenile (CM 566), including partial limbs.

facts.statement: In 1905, the American Museum of Natural History unveiled the first mounted sauropod skeleton, a composite specimen named Brontosaurus excelsus.
facts.quote: In 1905, the American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) unveiled the first-ever mounted skeleton of a sauropod, a composite specimen (mainly made of bones from AMNH 460) that they referred to as Brontosaurus excelsus.

facts.statement: An Apatosaurus skull was discovered in 1909 during the first expedition to the Carnegie Quarry at Dinosaur National Monument, led by Earl Douglass.
facts.quote: In 1909, an Apatosaurus skull was found, during the first expedition to what would become the Carnegie Quarry at Dinosaur National Monument, led by Earl Douglass.

facts.statement: After William J. Holland died in 1934, museum staff placed a cast of a Camarasaurus skull on the Carnegie Quarry mount.
facts.quote: After Holland's death in 1934, a cast of a Camarasaurus skull was placed on the mount by museum staff.

facts.statement: On October 20, 1979, the Carnegie Museum mounted the first Apatosaurus skull on a skeleton following publications by McIntosh and Berman.
facts.quote: On October 20, 1979, after the publications by McIntosh and Berman, the first skull of an Apatosaurus was mounted on a skeleton in a museum, that of the Carnegie.

facts.statement: In 2011, the first Apatosaurus specimen with a skull articulated to its cervical vertebrae was described.
facts.quote: In 2011, the first specimen of Apatosaurus where a skull was found articulated with its cervical vertebrae was described.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus was a large, quadrupedal animal with a long neck, a whip-like tail, and forelimbs slightly shorter than its hindlimbs.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus was a large, long-necked, quadrupedal animal with a long, whip-like tail, and forelimbs that were slightly shorter than its hindlimbs.

facts.statement: The largest Brontosaurus species, B. excelsus, measured 21 to 23 meters long and weighed 15 to 20 tonnes, while other species measured 19 meters and weighed 14 tonnes.
facts.quote: The largest species, B. excelsus, measured up to 21 - 23 m long from head to tail and weighed up to 15 - 20 t; other species were smaller, measuring 19 m long and weighing 14 MT.

facts.statement: In 1902, Olof A. Peterson and Charles Gilmore named the juvenile and adult skeletons Elosaurus parvus.
facts.quote: The skeletons were granted a new genus and species name, Elosaurus parvus ("little field lizard"), by Olof A. Peterson and Charles Gilmore in 1902.

facts.statement: Several authors later transferred the species from Elosaurus to the genus Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: The species was later transferred to Apatosaurus by several authors.

facts.statement: In 2015, Tschopp et al. placed the species in the genus Brontosaurus during a comprehensive study of Diplodocidae.
facts.quote: The species was placed in Brontosaurus Tschopp et al. in 2015 during their comprehensive study of Diplodocidae.

facts.statement: In 2015, Tschopp, Mateus, and Benson concluded that Brontosaurus is a valid genus distinct from Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2015, an extensive study of diplodocid relationships by Emanuel Tschopp, Octavio Mateus, and Roger Benson concluded that Brontosaurus was indeed a valid genus of sauropod distinct from Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: Robert T. Bakker argued in the 1990s that A. excelsus merits a separate genus distinct from A. ajax.
facts.quote: Despite this, at least one paleontologist—Robert T. Bakker—argued in the 1990s that A. ajax and A. excelsus are sufficiently distinct that the latter continues to merit a separate genus.

facts.statement: Paleontologists John and ReBecca Foster continue to consider Brontosaurus a synonym of Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: Some paleontologists, such as John and ReBecca Foster, continue to consider Brontosaurus as a synonym of Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: The original AMNH Brontosaurus mount featured a sculpted skull based on Camarasaurus bones, which was later found to be inaccurate compared to the delicate Diplodocus-like skull.
facts.quote: In addition, a sculpted model of what the museum felt the skull of this massive creature might have looked like was placed on the skeleton. This was not a delicate skull like that of Diplodocus, which would later turn out to be more accurate, but was based on "the biggest, thickest, strongest skull bones, lower jaws, and tooth crowns from three different quarries".

facts.statement: McIntosh and Berman found that Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus likely had a Diplodocus-like skull, supporting Holland's earlier view.
facts.quote: They found that though he never published his opinion, Holland was almost certainly correct in that Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus had a Diplodocus-like skull.

facts.statement: The skull of Brontosaurus has never been found, but it is likely similar to that of the closely related Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: Although the skull of Brontosaurus has not been found, it was probably similar to the skull of the closely related Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus possessed spatulate, chisel-like teeth adapted for a herbivorous diet.
facts.quote: Jaws of Apatosaurus and other diplodocids were lined with spatulate (chisel-like) teeth which were adapted for herbivory.

facts.statement: The neck vertebrae of Brontosaurus were deeply bifurcated on the dorsal side, carrying paired spines that created a wide and deep neck.
facts.quote: Like those of other diplodocids, the vertebrae of the neck were deeply bifurcated on the dorsal side; that is, they carried paired spines, resulting in a wide and deep neck.

facts.statement: Vertebrae in the neck, torso, and sacrum of Brontosaurus had large pneumatic foramina on their lateral sides to lighten the bones.
facts.quote: Vertebrae in the neck, torso, and sacrum of sauropods bore large pneumatic foramina on their lateral sides. These are used to lighten the bones which aided in keeping the animal lighter.

facts.statement: Despite being pneumatic, the neck of Brontosaurus is thought to have been twice as massive as that of other diplodocids due to its sturdiness.
facts.quote: Despite its pneumaticy, the neck of Brontosaurus is thought to have been double the mass of that of other diplodocids due to the former's sturdiness.

facts.statement: The dorsal ribs of Brontosaurus were not fused or tightly attached to the vertebrae but were loosely articulated.
facts.quote: The dorsal ribs are not fused or tightly attached to their vertebrae, instead being loosely articulated.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus had ten dorsal ribs on each side of its body.
facts.quote: Ten dorsal ribs are on either side of the body.

facts.statement: The tail of Brontosaurus was comparatively slender, typical of diplodocids, because vertebral spines decreased in height rapidly away from the hips.
facts.quote: The shape of the tail was typical of diplodocids, being comparatively slender, due to the vertebral spines rapidly decreasing in height the farther they are from the hips.

facts.statement: The tail of Brontosaurus ended in a whip-like structure, as seen in other diplodocids.
facts.quote: As in other diplodocids, the last portion of the tail of Brontosaurus possessed a whip-like structure.

facts.statement: The scapula of Brontosaurus has a rounded extension off its edge, a characteristic unique to the genus among Apatosaurinae.
facts.quote: The scapula of Brontosaurus also has a rounded extension off of its edge, a characteristic unique to Brontosaurus among Apatosaurinae.

facts.statement: Charles Gilmore noted in 1936 that the radius and ulna of Brontosaurus remained parallel in life, contrary to earlier reconstructions suggesting they crossed.
facts.quote: Charles Gilmore in 1936 noted that previous reconstructions erroneously proposed that the radius and ulna could cross, when in life they would have remained parallel.

facts.statement: The phalangeal formula of Brontosaurus is 2-1-1-1-1, meaning the innermost finger has two bones and the subsequent fingers have one bone each.
facts.quote: The phalangeal formula is 2-1-1-1-1, meaning the innermost finger (phalanx) on the forelimb has two bones and the next has one.

facts.statement: Originally described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879, Brontosaurus was long considered a junior synonym of Apatosaurus, with its type species reclassified as Apatosaurus excelsus in 1903.
facts.quote: Originally named by its discoverer Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879, Brontosaurus had long been considered a junior synonym of Apatosaurus; its type species, Brontosaurus excelsus, was reclassified as A. excelsus in 1903.

facts.statement: A 2015 study concluded that Brontosaurus is a valid genus distinct from Apatosaurus, though this classification is not agreed upon by all paleontologists.
facts.quote: However, an extensive study published in 2015 by a joint British-Portuguese research team concluded that Brontosaurus was a valid genus of sauropod distinct from Apatosaurus. Nevertheless, not all paleontologists agree with this division.

facts.statement: The type species Brontosaurus excelsus was first named by Othniel Marsh in 1879.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus excelsus, the type species of Brontosaurus, was first named by Marsh in 1879.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus parvus was originally described as Elosaurus in 1902 by Peterson and Gilmore before being reassigned to Brontosaurus in 2015.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus parvus, first described as Elosaurus in 1902 by Peterson and Gilmore, was reassigned to Apatosaurus in 1994, and to Brontosaurus in 2015.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus yahnahpin is the oldest known species, dating to approximately 155 million years ago.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus yahnahpin is the oldest species, known from a single site from the lower Morrison Formation, Bertha Quarry, in Albany County, Wyoming, dating to about 155 million years ago.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus yahnahpin was originally described by James Filla and Patrick Redman in 1994 as a species of Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: It was described by James Filla and Patrick Redman in 1994 as a species of Apatosaurus (A. yahnahpin).

facts.statement: Brontosaurus parvus dates to the middle Kimmeridgian age.
facts.quote: It dates to the middle Kimmeridgian.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus was originally named by its discoverer Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus fue originalmente nombrado por su descubridor Othniel Charles Marsh en 1879.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus species lived between 155 and 152 million years ago in the lower to middle Kimmeridgian of the Morrison Formation in Wyoming and Utah.
facts.quote: Las especies de Brontosaurus se extienden en un rango temporal de 155 a 152 millones de años, durante la época del Kimmeridgiense de la zona inferior a media de la Formación Morrison en Wyoming y Utah, en Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: B. yahnahpin grew up to 21 meters long.
facts.quote: It grew up to 21 m long.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus amplus is a junior synonym of B. excelsus.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus amplus, is a junior synonym of B. excelsus.

facts.statement: The genus Brontosaurus was established by Marsh in 1879.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Marsh, 1879

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Brontosaurus is B. excelsus.
facts.quote: type_species: Brontosaurus excelsus

facts.statement: The genus Brontosaurus includes the species B. parvus and B. yahnahpin.
facts.quote: subdivision: Brontosaurus parvus (, 1902) Brontosaurus yahnahpin (, 1994)

facts.statement: Elosaurus and Eobrontosaurus are listed as synonyms of Brontosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Elosaurus Peterson & Gilmore, 1902 Eobrontosaurus Bakker, 1998

facts.statement: A 2015 study concluded that Brontosaurus is a valid genus distinct from Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un extenso estudio publicado en 2015 concluyó que Brontosaurus es un género válido de saurópodo y distinto de Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: Marsh originally suggested Brontosaurus lacked intellect based on its small braincase and slender neural cord.
facts.quote: Marsh also noted the animal's supposed lack of intellect based on the small braincase of the Felch Quarry skull and slender neural cord.

facts.statement: The single claw on sauropod forelimbs was likely not used for defense due to its shape and size.
facts.quote: Various uses for the single claw on the forelimb of sauropods have been proposed. One suggestion is that they were used for defense, but their shape and size make this unlikely.

facts.statement: The most probable use for the sauropod forelimb claw was grasping objects like tree trunks when rearing.
facts.quote: It was also possible they were for foraging, but the most probable use for the claw was grasping objects such as tree trunks when rearing.

facts.statement: Trackways suggest Brontosaurus traveled an average of 20-40 km per day and could reach speeds of 20-30 km/h.
facts.quote: Trackways of sauropods like Brontosaurus show that the average range for them was around 20 - 40 km per day, and they could potentially reach a top speed of 20 - 30 km/h.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus teeth were replaced entirely at once and up to 60% more frequently than Diplodocus teeth.
facts.quote: The replacement method and physiology of Apatosauruss teeth is unique, with the entire tooth row being replaced at once and up to 60% more often than Diplodocus.

facts.statement: The tooth characteristics of Apatosaurus and likely Brontosaurus imply they consumed tougher vegetation than Diplodocus.
facts.quote: These characteristics imply that Apatosaurus, and likely Brontosaurus, consumed tougher vegetation than Diplodocus.

facts.statement: If Brontosaurus was an endotherm, fewer adults could be sustained compared to if it were an ectotherm, which could support tens of animals per square kilometer.
facts.quote: If Brontosaurus was an endotherm, fewer adult individuals could be sustained than if it were an ectotherm, which could have tens of animals per square kilometer.

facts.statement: It has been theorized that Brontosaurus migrated between feeding sites to meet dietary needs in the arid Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: Due to this, it has been theorized that Brontosaurus and other sauropods living within the arid environment of the Morrison Formation participated in migrations between feeding sites.

facts.statement: Assuming an avian respiratory system and reptilian metabolism, Frank Paladino et al. (1997) estimated Brontosaurus needed about 262 liters of water per day.
facts.quote: Assuming Apatosaurus had an avian respiratory system and a reptilian resting-metabolism, Frank Paladino etal. (1997) estimate the animal would have needed to consume only about 262 L of water per day.

facts.statement: Historically, it was believed Brontosaurus was too massive to live on dry land and must have lived partly submerged in water.
facts.quote: Historically, sauropods like Brontosaurus were believed to have been too massive to support their weight on dry land, so theoretically, they must have lived partly submerged in water, perhaps in swamps.

facts.statement: Recent findings indicate sauropods were fully terrestrial animals, contradicting the theory that they lived partly submerged.
facts.quote: Recent findings do not support this, and sauropods are thought to have been fully terrestrial animals.

facts.statement: Diplodocids like Brontosaurus are often portrayed with necks held high to browse on tall trees.
facts.quote: Diplodocids like Brontosaurus are often portrayed with their necks held high up in the air, allowing them to browse on tall trees.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that sauropods were semi-aquatic and lethargic is unsupported by fossil evidence, suggesting they were active terrestrial animals.
facts.quote: This is unsupported by fossil evidence. Instead, sauropods were active and had adaptations for dwelling on land.

facts.statement: There is debate over whether Brontosaurus was an ectotherm or endotherm, affecting hypotheses about its population density and distribution.
facts.quote: Estimations of the dietary necessities of Brontosaurus were made in 2010, with a guess of 2e4 to 50e4 kJ needed daily. This led to hypotheses on the distributions of Brontosaurus to meet this requirement, though they varied on whether it was an ectotherm or endotherm.

facts.statement: Studies disagree on sauropod neck posture, with some suggesting limited flexibility and others arguing they held necks at maximum vertical extension.
facts.quote: Though some studies have suggested that diplodocid necks were less flexible than previously believed, other studies have found that all tetrapods appear to hold their necks at the maximum possible vertical extension when in a normal, alert posture, and argue that the same would hold true for sauropods barring any unknown, unique characteristics that set the soft tissue anatomy of their necks apart from that of other animals.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus was a large quadruped with a long neck and a long whip-like tail.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus era un animal cuadrúpedo grande dotado de un cuello largo y larga cola en forma de látigo.

facts.statement: Its front legs were slightly shorter than its hind legs.
facts.quote: Sus patas delanteras eran levemente más cortas que las traseras.

facts.statement: The largest species, B. excelsus, weighed over 15 tonnes and measured over 22 meters in length from head to tail.
facts.quote: La especie más grande, B. excelsus, pesaba más de 15 toneladas y medía más de 22 metros de longitud de la cabeza a la cola.

facts.statement: The skull has not been found, but it is likely similar to that of its close relative Apatosaurus louisae.
facts.quote: El cráneo no ha sido hallado, pero probablemente era parecido al de su pariente cercano Apatosaurus louisae.

facts.statement: Like other sauropods, Brontosaurus had bifurcated neck vertebrae with a pair of spines on each side, resulting in a wide and thick neck.
facts.quote: Como ocurre en otros saurópodos, las vértebras del cuello se encontraban bifurcadas; es decir, poseían un par de espinas a los lados, dando como resultado un cuello ancho y grueso.

facts.statement: The vertebral formula consists of 15 cervical, 10 dorsal, 5 sacral, and 82 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: La fórmula vertebral es: 15 cervicales, 10 dorsales, 5 sacrales y 82 caudales.

facts.statement: There is notable variation in the number of caudal vertebrae, even within the same species.
facts.quote: Es notoria la variación en el número de vértebras caudales, incluso dentro de una misma especie.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae were more robust than in other diplodocids, though not to the same extent as in adult Apatosaurus specimens.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales eran más robustas que en otros diplodócidos, aunque no en el mismo grado que en los ejemplares adultos de Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: There were ten dorsal ribs on each side of the body.
facts.quote: Hay diez costillas dorsales a cada lado del cuerpo.

facts.statement: The neck possessed an extensive system of air sacs that lightened it.
facts.quote: El cuello poseía un extenso sistema de sacos aéreos que lo aligeraban.

facts.statement: Like its relative Apatosaurus, Brontosaurus had high spines on its vertebrae, which accounted for more than half the height of the individual bones.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus, como su pariente Apatosaurus tenía espinas altas en sus vértebras, las cuales suponían más de la mitad de la altura de los huesos individuales.

facts.statement: The tail shape was unusual for a diplodocid, being comparatively thin due to the rapid decrease in vertebral spine height as they moved away from the hips.
facts.quote: La forma de la cola era inusual para ser un diplodócido, al ser comparativamente delgada, debido al rápido descenso de la altura de las espinas vertebrales a medida que se alejaban de las caderas.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus also had very long ribs compared to many other diplodocids, giving them unusually high torsos.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus además tenían costillas muy largas comparadas con muchos otros diplodócidos, lo que les daba torsos inusualmente altos.

facts.statement: Like other members of its family, the posterior section of Brontosaurus's tail had a whip-like structure.
facts.quote: Como en otros miembros de su familia, la sección posterior de la cola de Brontosaurus poseía una estructura en forma de látigo.

facts.statement: Charles Gilmore noted in 1936 that earlier reconstructions incorrectly suggested the radius and ulna could cross, whereas in life they could only remain parallel.
facts.quote: Charles Gilmore señaló en 1936 que las reconstrucciones anteriores proponían de manera errónea que el radio y el cúbito podían cruzarse, cuando en vida solo podían permanecer en paralelo.

facts.statement: Brontosaurus had a single large claw on each front foot, while only the first three toes on its hind foot had claws.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus tenía una única gran garra en cada pata delantera, mientras que en su pie solo los primeros tres dedos tenían garras.

facts.statement: The manual claw bone had a slight curvature and shortened just at the front tip.
facts.quote: El hueso de la garra manual tiene una curvatura leve, y se acortaba justamente en el extremo frontal.

facts.statement: The hip bones included a robust ilium, and the pubis and ischium were fused.
facts.quote: Los huesos de la cadera incluían un robusto ilion, y el pubis e isquion fusionados.

facts.statement: The tibia and fibula bones in the hind leg were different from the slender bones of Diplodocus but were very similar to those of Camarasaurus.
facts.quote: Los huesos de la tibia y el peroné en la pata posterior eran diferentes de los delgados huesos de Diplodocus, pero son sumamente similares a los de Camarasaurus.

facts.statement: The fibula was longer than the tibia, although it was also thinner.
facts.quote: El peroné es más largo que la tibia, aunque también es más delgado.

facts.statement: In 1879, Othniel C. Marsh announced the discovery of a large and fairly complete sauropod skeleton from rocks of the Morrison Formation in Como Bluff, Wyoming.
facts.quote: En 1879, Othniel C. Marsh, un profesor de paleontología de la Universidad de Yale, anunció el descubrimiento de un esqueleto de un saurópodo grande y bastante completo de rocas de la Formación Morrison en Como Bluff, Wyoming.

facts.statement: He identified it as belonging to a completely new genus and species, naming it Brontosaurus excelsus, meaning "thunder lizard" from Greek and "noble" or "high" from Latin.
facts.quote: Lo identificó como perteneciente a un género y especie completamente nuevos, a los que nombró como Brontosaurus excelsus, que significa "lagarto trueno", del griego brontē/βροντη que significa "trueno" y sauros/σαυρος que significa "lagarto", y el latín excelsus, "noble" o "alto".

facts.statement: In 1903, Elmer Riggs claimed Brontosaurus was not distinct enough from Apatosaurus to warrant its own genus, creating the new combination Apatosaurus excelsus.
facts.quote: Elmer Riggs, en la edición de 1903 de la revista Geological Series of the Field Columbian Museum, afirmó que Brontosaurus no era lo bastante distinto de Apatosaurus como para garantizar su propio género, por lo que creó la nueva combinación Apatosaurus excelsus.

facts.statement: Riggs established that "in view of these facts the two genera can be considered as synonyms. Since the term 'Apatosaurus' has priority, 'Brontosaurus' will be considered as a synonym".
facts.quote: Riggs estableció que "En vista de estos hechos los dos géneros pueden ser considerados como sinónimos. Ya que el término 'Apatosaurus' tiene prioridad, 'Brontosaurus' será considerado como un sinónimo".

facts.statement: In 1905, the American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) revealed the first mounted sauropod skeleton, a composite specimen mainly formed from the bones of AMNH 460, referred to the species Brontosaurus excelsus.
facts.quote: En 1905, el Museo Americano de Historia Natural (AMNH) reveló el primer esqueleto montado de un saurópodo, un espécimen compuesto, mayormente formado de los huesos de AMNH 460, que fue referido a la especie Brontosaurus excelsus.

facts.statement: To complete the mount, the rest of the tail was modeled to have the appearance Marsh believed it should have, which had very few vertebrae.
facts.quote: Para completar la montura, el resto de la cola fue modelada para que tuviera la apariencia que Marsh creía debía tener, la cual tenía muy pocas vértebras.

facts.statement: Additionally, a sculpted model of what museum authorities thought the skull of the immense creature should be was placed on the skeleton.
facts.quote: Además de esto, se colocó en el esqueleto un modelo esculpido de como pensaban las autoridades del museo que debía ser el cráneo de la inmensa criatura.

facts.statement: This was not a delicate skull like that of Diplodocus, which was later shown to be more correct, but was based on "larger, thicker, and stronger cranial bones, jaws, and dental crowns from three different quarries".
facts.quote: Este no era un cráneo delicado como el de Diplodocus, el cual más tarde se mostraría que es más correcto, sino que estaba basado en "los huesos craneales, mandíbulas y coronas dentales más grandes, gruesas y fuertes de tres canteras diferentes".

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn noted in a publication that the skull was "mostly a conjecture and based on that of Morosaurus", now Camarasaurus.
facts.quote: Henry Fairfield Osborn señaló en una publicación que el cráneo era "mayormente una conjetura y basado en el de Morosaurus", ahora Camarasaurus.
